RFC 6962 states that Certificate Transparency logs use a binary Merkle Hash Tree with SHA-256 as the hashing algorithm.
RFC 8446 states that TLS 1.3 removes static RSA and Diffie-Hellman cipher suites so all public-key based key exchange mechanisms provide forward secrecy.
RFC 793 specifies that TCP uses a three-way handshake mechanism when establishing a connection.
RFC 9110 states that HTTP request methods are considered safe if their defined semantics are essentially read-only without expected state change on the origin server.
RFC 8259 states that JSON text exchanged between systems not part of a closed ecosystem MUST be encoded using UTF-8.
RFC 4648 specifies that Base64 uses a 65-character subset of US-ASCII enabling 6 bits per printable character, with = as the extra 65th character.
The archived December 2009 Wikipedia revision describes hash trees (or Merkle trees) as a data structure used in cryptography and computer science.
